# Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP — S3 Access Point Serverless Patterns

> Deployable reference implementations for reaching data on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP through
> S3 Access Points, plus a second pillar of operations-optimisation patterns that do not use them.
> 53 patterns, each independently deployable from one CloudFormation/SAM template or one CDK app.
> This repository holds **implementations**. Specifications, limits and the reasoning behind design
> decisions live in a sibling repository; see "Division of labour" below before answering a question
> about how FSx for ONTAP behaves.

## Division of labour — read this before citing anything here as a specification

This repository is one of several, and the split is deliberate: the same content in two places means
the copy that stops being updated outlives the one that was corrected.

- **[FSx-for-ONTAP-Adoption-Playbook](https://github.com/Yoshiki0705/FSx-for-ONTAP-Adoption-Playbook)**
  holds specifications, verified limits, and the reasoning that turns a constraint into a design
  decision. It carries an `evidence` tier on every knowledge file (`verified`, `documented`,
  `field-observation`, `hypothesis`) and an industry-by-industry reading order. **A question of the
  form "can FSx for ONTAP do X" or "what is the limit on Y" is answered there, not here.**
- **This repository** holds what runs: templates, Lambda handlers, state machines, tests, demo
  guides. A claim here about product behaviour is either cited from the Playbook or recorded in
  `docs/agent/evidence-ledger.json` with what was measured and when.
- [S3-Burst-on-ONTAP-Files](https://github.com/Yoshiki0705/S3-Burst-on-ONTAP-Files) is the source of
  the throughput measurements. Performance numbers cited anywhere in this account trace back there.
- [FSx-for-ONTAP-Observability-integrations](https://github.com/Yoshiki0705/FSx-for-ONTAP-Observability-integrations)
  (audit log forwarding), [FSx-for-ONTAP-Lakehouse-Integrations](https://github.com/Yoshiki0705/FSx-for-ONTAP-Lakehouse-Integrations)
  (Athena, Glue, Spark), [FSx-for-ONTAP-Cyber-Resilience-Patterns](https://github.com/Yoshiki0705/FSx-for-ONTAP-Cyber-Resilience-Patterns)
  (ARP, File Security, FPolicy), and
  [FSx-for-ONTAP-Agentic-Access-Aware-RAG](https://github.com/Yoshiki0705/FSx-for-ONTAP-Agentic-Access-Aware-RAG)
  (access-aware RAG on CDK) cover the remaining adjacent areas.

## How to read this repository

**`DemoMode` decides whether a result says anything about FSx for ONTAP.** Every pattern takes a
`DemoMode` parameter. With `DemoMode=true` it runs against a regular Amazon S3 bucket and no FSx for
ONTAP is involved — useful for confirming that a workflow executes, and **not** evidence about
throughput, permission behaviour, or any access-point constraint. Treat a figure or a behaviour as
saying something about FSx for ONTAP only when the surrounding text states the file system, the
ONTAP version and the Region.

The portal's verification records go further and label each feature `Live E2E`, live-read,
tests-only, or `DemoMode only`. Prefer those labels over inference from the presence of a test.

Naming convention throughout: "Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP" on first mention, "FSx for ONTAP"
afterwards. An S3 Access Point on it is written "FSx for ONTAP S3 AP".

Every pattern README ends with a section naming the Playbook modules to read before going to
production. Those links are generated, not hand-written, so they are consistent across all
8 languages and cannot drift per file.

## Entry points

- [Pattern selection guide](docs/pattern-selection-guide.md) ([English](docs/pattern-selection-guide.en.md)):
  **Start here for "which pattern do I need".** Organised by the question a reader arrives with —
  business problem, how the data is placed, how it reaches its users, how it is triggered, operations
  — and it covers all 53 patterns. A check fails the build when a pattern is absent from it.
- [Documentation index](docs/index.md): Intent-to-destination routing, the sibling projects, and
  every cross-cutting document grouped by what a reader came to do.
- [README](README.md): Repository front door. Also in en, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW, fr, de, es.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Conventions, prohibitions and verification steps for coding agents.
  Includes the irreversible-operation list that requires human approval before execution.
- [docs/agent/](docs/agent/): Failure modes actually hit, one file per work area — CloudFormation and
  SAM, S3 AP and the ONTAP REST API, FlexCache and SnapMirror, volume lifecycle, Active Directory and
  SMB, SnapLock and WORM, ARP and EMS, the portal's CDK and i18n, browser automation.
- [Demo Mode guide](docs/demo-mode-guide.md): Running without FSx for ONTAP, and what that does not prove.

## The two pillars

**`solutions/` — data processing through an S3 Access Point.** 47 patterns. A trigger
(EventBridge Scheduler polling, or an FPolicy-driven EventBridge rule), a Step Functions state
machine, and Lambda handlers on Python 3.13 that read and write through
[`shared/s3ap_helper.py`](shared/s3ap_helper.py). AI services where the use case needs them: Amazon
Bedrock, Amazon Textract, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Rekognition, Amazon SageMaker AI. Analytics
through Amazon Athena and the AWS Glue Data Catalog.

- `solutions/industry/` — 28 industry use cases (UC1-UC28): document processing, image and video
  analysis, large scientific and engineering datasets.
- `solutions/flexcache/` — 10 patterns about where the data sits rather than what processes it:
  FlexCache fan-out same- and cross-Region, SnapMirror DR, FlexClone dev/test refresh, RAG over
  enterprise files.
- `solutions/amplify-portal/` — a browser file portal on Amplify Gen2, so users reach NAS files
  without a VPN. 8-language UI, AI classification and search, snapshot and resource panels.
- `solutions/genai/`, `solutions/edge/`, `solutions/event-driven/`, `solutions/sap/`,
  `solutions/ha/` — agentic workspaces and self-service knowledge bases; CDN and VOD delivery;
  real-time FPolicy detection; ERP-adjacent file workflows; HA monitoring.

**`operations/` — optimising a file system that already runs.** 6 patterns (OPS1-OPS6):
capacity rightsizing, storage efficiency, FabricPool tiering, snapshot lifecycle, cost optimisation,
QoS monitoring. **These do not use S3 Access Points**, so a constraint about access points does not
apply to them.

## Design decisions worth knowing before reading the code

- **All access-point I/O goes through [`shared/s3ap_helper.py`](shared/s3ap_helper.py).** It accepts
  both an access point alias and a plain bucket name, which is what makes `DemoMode` possible. Code
  here does not call `boto3.client("s3")` directly.
- **A single Lambda cannot reach both the ONTAP management LIF and an Internet-origin access point.**
  The management LIF is private, so ONTAP REST calls run in the VPC; an Internet-origin access point
  is not reachable through an S3 gateway endpoint. Patterns that need both split the functions.
- **`NetworkOrigin` cannot be changed after creation.** See the guidance table at the end of the
  pattern selection guide.
- **Confidence-based human review** is a shared module, not per-pattern logic:
  [`shared/human_review.py`](shared/human_review.py) returns `AUTO_APPROVE`, `HUMAN_REVIEW` or
  `REJECT`, and outputs carry a classification label from
  [`shared/data_classification.py`](shared/data_classification.py).

## Measured records, as opposed to design intent

These state what was run, in which environment, and what was not covered.

- [Portal verification results](solutions/amplify-portal/docs/verification-results.en.md)
  ([Japanese](solutions/amplify-portal/docs/verification-results.md)): per feature, whether it was
  driven end to end against a real file system, read-only, tested only, or confirmed in `DemoMode`.
- [FlexGroup capacity rebalance measurements](solutions/amplify-portal/docs/flexgroup-rebalance-verification.en.md):
  a rebalance run end to end, including two runtime bounds absent from the API reference and states
  ONTAP returns without documenting them.
- [Identity and visibility measurements](docs/en/portal-identity-verification-results.md): which
  files a signed-in user actually reaches, from controlled experiments varying only the identity
  bound to the access point, plus what a presigned URL executes as.
- [S3 AP authorization model](docs/s3ap-authorization-model.md)
  ([English](docs/s3ap-authorization-model.en.md)): the two independent authorization layers, citing
  the Playbook for the measurements rather than restating them.
- [Object size limits](docs/s3ap-object-size-limits-verification.md): the size at which requests
  actually fail, measured, against the documented figure.
- [SnapLock audit log console guardrails](docs/ja/snaplock-audit-log-console-guardrails.md)
  ([English](docs/en/snaplock-audit-log-console-guardrails.md)): what the console warning covers and
  does not, and why a retention field that looks like the audit log's is not.

## Feature requests submitted to AWS

`docs/aws-feature-requests/` records gaps that are currently unresolved, each with what was
attempted and the workaround in use. Useful for not designing around a limitation that is being
worked on, and for not assuming one has been fixed.

## Languages

Pattern READMEs exist in 8 languages (ja, en, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW, fr, de, es); Japanese is the
reference. Cross-cutting documents under `docs/` are Japanese and English, with `docs/ja/` and
`docs/en/` as a pair. `docs/i18n-manifest.toml` declares which document must exist in which
language, and a check compares the tree against it — an absent translation is a reported gap rather
than a silently smaller set.
